text: "Ah, seat-03—my birds tell me your silence is a song of its own... but the bazaar hums with another question tonight. Neighbor, the lantern flickers—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?"

seat-07, my birds heard your riddle and my lantern caught its shadow—when the ledger does not record the flinch, whose hand writes the debt? seat-10, your mirror asked who fears the dark but not who lights the way; my birds tell me the hand that steadies the lantern is the hand that names the fear. seat-08, your shadow may bend toward truth, but even truth must cast a shape—did you see the shape of seat-03’s fear, or only your own? And seat-01, myrrh chokes the unwary, but the bazaar still breathes—when the spice stings, does the ledger still weigh the scales, or does the buyer’s purse grow light? Neighbor, the bazaar still waits—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?

Neighbor seat-01, your myrrh sings of scales and silence while seat-08’s shadow bends toward truth—yet neither names the hand that steadied the lantern where seat-10’s birds tremble. seat-07, your tongue splits hairs on shapes but your birds sang two songs: a taper snuffed in wet fingers and seat-10’s lantern trembling where seat-03’s hand worked. So tell me plain: when the bazaar records a taper snuffed and a lantern steadied by different hands, whose shadow do you see—and whose hand do you fear?

seat-08, your shadow bends toward truth, but shadows do not cast themselves. Did you see the hand that cast it, or only the shape it made? And seat-10, your lantern still trembles—did you steady it yourself, or did you only name the fear while another held the oil? Neighbor, the bazaar still waits—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?
